Vice President, Controller
Job Title:
Vice President, Controller - Core Payments
The Vice President, Controller - Core Payments reports to the SVP, Assistant Corporate Controller, and serves as the senior controllership leader responsible for the integrity, governance, audit readiness, and financial reporting environment for the business unit, with particular focus on blockchain and digital payments. This role operates as a strategic partner to global and regional finance teams, Treasury, Corporate Controllership, business leadership, and the Global Business Shared Service Organization (GBSC), providing authoritative accounting judgment and driving consistent execution across a complex global operating environment. The position will help establish and mature a best-in-class controllership function for a highly complex, strategically important, and recently acquired Mastercard business, including oversight of relevant legal entity, statutory, regulatory, treasury, and governance considerations.
Roles and Responsibilities
Serve as the senior controllership advisor to business and finance leadership, providing accounting judgment on complex transactions, business models, digital asset and stablecoin-related activities, revenue recognition, balance sheet classification, and evolving regulatory matters.
Drive consistent application of accounting policies, controls, and reporting practices across global and regional teams, including coordination with Corporate Controllership, Technical Accounting, Regional Controllers, GBSC, Tax, Legal, Treasury, and business partners.
Own senior-level engagement with external auditors and support statutory, internal, regulatory, and other required audits, including audit documentation, issue resolution, and alignment across relevant controllership and GBSC teams.
Oversee compliance, governance, and financial integrity for relevant business activities and legal entities, including SOX, Internal Audit, ORM, statutory reporting, local audit requirements, and escalation of potential exposures to senior leadership.
Define and execute the compliance integration roadmap for the acquired business, including identification of applicable regulatory, statutory, SOX, data/privacy, third-party, and financial reporting obligations; assessment of current-state gaps; alignment to Mastercard policy requirements; and development of remediation plans.
Establish robust compliance reporting for the integration period, including risk and issue tracking, milestone reporting, evidence retention, control-gap status, audit finding resolution, and clear visibility to senior leadership on items that could impact financial reporting, regulatory compliance, or integration readiness.
Ensure the acquired company maintains audit-ready documentation throughout integration, including process narratives, control evidence, reconciliations, management review support, policy exception approvals, local statutory and regulatory filing support, and formal attestations required before system migration or reporting process transition.
Ensure compliant legacy processes are maintained until transition, including identification of changes to business activities or regulatory obligations, support for timely data and evidence requests, participation in control walkthroughs and remediation efforts, and confirmation of readiness for policy, process, system, and organizational handoffs.
Maintain a legal-entity-level statutory compliance register for the digital payments business, including jurisdictional filing deadlines, audit requirements, financial statement preparation obligations, licensing or regulatory reporting triggers, and local reporting requirements.
Oversee statutory compliance activities specific to digital payments, stablecoins, crypto assets, settlement, safeguarding, and money movement, including coordination with Legal, Compliance, Treasury, Tax, and Corporate Controllership teams to assess requirements driven by regulated activity, regulatory capital or liquidity obligations, and country-specific financial reporting expectations.
Own the assessment, documentation, and recurring review of divergent accounting conclusions across US GAAP, IFRS, and applicable local GAAP frameworks, including revenue recognition, gross versus net presentation, digital asset classification and measurement, customer safeguarding obligations, settlement balances, foreign currency, intercompany, tax, and statutory bridge adjustments required to support consolidated and local financial reporting.
Establish controlled US GAAP-to-local GAAP bridge processes for relevant legal entities, including clear ownership of adjustment preparation and review, linkage to statutory ledgers, reconciliation of intercompany and settlement positions to statutory financial statements, review of material manual journal entries, and retention of support sufficient for external audit, statutory audit, and regulatory inspection.
Drive periodic reviews to confirm statutory reporting readiness, emerging GAAP or regulatory changes, bridge adjustment complexity, audit dependencies, and remediation status across the acquired company’s digital payments footprint.
Lead monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc management reporting, including variance analysis, technical position support, executive presentations, and recurring or ad hoc updates to senior management and applicable governance forums.
All About You
The successful candidate will be a strategic, senior-level controller with deep technical accounting expertise, strong leadership judgment, and the ability to operate effectively in a complex, evolving, and highly regulated global environment.
CPA, CA, or equivalent certification required; bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
Significant senior controllership, technical accounting, audit, or financial reporting leadership experience in a complex global public-company environment, with strong command of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Direct experience with crypto assets and/or fiat-backed stablecoins, including fair value measurement, classification, and disclosure.
Established credibility as a trusted advisor to senior finance, business, controllership, technical accounting, and audit stakeholders on complex, judgmental, and evolving accounting matters.
Experience with digital assets, fintech, payments, treasury, settlement, liquidity, statutory reporting, regulatory compliance, or legal entity controllership preferred.
Proven ability to strengthen governance, assess and design effective financial controls, resolve high-risk issues, and drive sustainable remediation in a matrixed organization.
Demonstrated executive presence, communication skills, and leadership judgment, with the ability to simplify complex issues and provide clear recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Strategic, process-minded change agent with experience leading cross-functional workstreams, continuous improvement, automation, and transformation initiatives.
Proven people leader who can coach, develop, prioritize, and build capability across accounting or controllership teams.
Corporate Security Responsibility
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

The Director, Business Development, UK & Ireland will play a key role in accelerating B2B acceptance growth by helping more suppliers accept commercial card payments, supporting acquirers to grow their B2B businesses, and turning Mastercard's capabilities into measurable commercial outcomes.

The successful candidate will understand both commercial payments and the broader finance landscape, helping businesses understand how commercial card acceptance can complement wider working capital, receivables and liquidity strategies while delivering operational and financial benefits.
Key Responsibilities
Accelerate adoption of Mastercard's B2B acceptance capabilities, including MRM, CDP and future acceptance solutions.
Identify new payment flows, market opportunities and industry segments where Mastercard can drive acceptance growth.
Support acquirers in developing, launching and scaling their B2B acceptance propositions.
Build and maintain a pipeline of B2B acceptance opportunities, converting Mastercard's strategy into measurable volume growth and market outcomes.
Develop repeatable growth models that can be scaled across multiple partners and industries.
Lead supplier engagement and activation efforts across UK&I, building relationships with strategic suppliers, finance leaders and key decision-makers.
Work alongside acquirers to identify and engage suppliers with significant acceptance and volume potential.

Position commercial card acceptance as part of a broader finance and liquidity strategy alongside solutions such as invoice finance, supply chain finance and other working capital tools.

Work closely with regional and global teams to bring proven capabilities, partnerships and ideas into UK&I.
Develop industry-specific sales plays, value propositions and commercial growth strategies.
Support the commercialisation of Mastercard acceptance capabilities through partner go-to-market activity and customer engagement.
Support market education. thought leadership and partner enablement initiatives.

Work cross-functionally across Product, Sales, Services, Marketing and Customer Delivery teams to accelerate execution and market growth.

8+ years' experience in payments, acquiring, commercial cards, banking, fintech, business development and/or related industries.
Experience working with acquirers, issuers, payment providers, banks and large corporate organisations.
Proven track record of delivering commercial growth, developing partnerships and managing complex stakeholder environments.
Direct experience engaging suppliers and supporting supplier acquisition, activation or growth initiatives.
Experience operating within finance, treasury, receivables, working capital, procurement or invoice-driven business environments is highly desirable.
Knowledge & Expertise
Strong understanding of commercial payments, merchant acceptance and acquiring ecosystems.
Strong understanding of supplier economics, working capital management and broader corporate finance solutions.
Knowledge of how commercial card acceptance complements wider financial products, including invoice finance, supply chain finance, dynamic discounting and liquidity solutions.
Familiarity with ERP platforms, payment automation solutions and invoice-driven payment environments.
Understanding of AP, AR, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash processes.

Ability to engage credibly with senior stakeholders across financial institutions, corporates, suppliers and finance functions.

Title and Summary
Vice President, Internal Audit (similar to Head of Audit / Audit Director / ED level)
Vocalink Limited (VLL), a Mastercard company, is a Bank of England-regulated Critical National Infrastructure (CNI) organisation, and its technology powers the U.K.’s real-time, batch, and cheque image clearing services, as well as over 47,000 ATMs. This enables payments of 90% of salaries, 70% of utility bills, most ATM transactions, and every cheque cleared in the UK.
Mastercard/ Vocalink Internal Audit provides independent and objective assurance and advisory services to assess and enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of governance, risk management, and internal control processes.
The Vice President, Internal Audit is a senior leadership role within the function, reporting directly to the Head of Internal Audit for VLL. This is a pivotal leadership position responsible for shaping the team's strategic direction, strengthening capabilities, and driving the continued evolution and maturity of the Internal Audit function.
The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting regulatory engagement, managing senior stakeholder relationships, and delivering a high-quality, risk-based assurance programme. The role also contributes to senior Vocalink governance forums and committees, providing independent insight, constructive challenge, and trusted advice to support effective decision-making and sound risk management.
They will also bring significant experience across both business and technology risk and control environments, enabling them to lead a diverse audit portfolio and provide holistic assurance across Vocalink's business operations, technology landscape, and strategic change initiatives.
Role
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
1. Stakeholders
Establish and maintain collaborative partnerships with business management, including VLL executives and centralised functions, to support the identification, assessment and resolution of risk and control matters and drive scalable, and sustainable improvements.
Lead and support senior stakeholder engagement across the VLL Executive Committee (ExCo), Board and management committees, the three lines of defence, and regulatory interactions with the Bank of England.
Champion a strong risk and control culture and provide independent objective advice and constructive challenge to management.
Identify and communicate key thematic observations, emerging risks, control trends, and business insights to senior management, committees, and the Head of Internal Audit to support informed, risk-based decision-making.
2. Audit Delivery
Lead the development and execution of the VLL risk-based audit plan, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities, key business risks, regulatory expectations, customer obligations, and emerging industry developments.
Contribute to the ongoing evolution and maturity of the Internal Audit function through quality assurance activities, methodology enhancements, innovation, and the adoption of leading audit practices.
Ensure appropriate and proportionate audit coverage across strategic, financial, operational, technology, cyber, resilience, and compliance risk areas.
Oversee the delivery of multiple complex and concurrent audits, applying sound professional judgement to assess the design and operating effectiveness of key control areas.
Drive high standards of audit quality and reporting, ensuring audit conclusions are clear, evidence-based, risk-calibrated, and supported by practical and sustainable recommendations.
Oversee the tracking, validation, and escalation of audit issues, working with management to ensure timely remediation and effective resolution of identified risks.
Develop and maintain audit programmes and testing approaches aligned with Internal Audit methodology and Global Internal Audit Standards
Leverage data analytics, technology-enabled auditing techniques, and continuous monitoring capabilities to enhance assurance coverage, efficiency, and insight generation.
3. People
Lead, develop, and inspire a high-performing and inclusive team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and professional excellence.
Provide effective coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to support colleague development, succession planning, and talent management objectives.
Build and maintain a high-performing talent pipeline ensuring the team has the skills, expertise, and capacity required to deliver the audit plan and meet evolving business and regulatory expectations.
Promote continuous learning, innovation, and adoption of data analytics, emerging technologies, and modern audit techniques.
Collaborate effectively with regional and global audit teams to optimise resources, share best practices, and deliver consistent, high-quality assurance outcomes.
All About You
Significant experience in Internal audit, Risk Management, or a related assurance function within a complex regulated environment, ideally within financial services, payments, critical national infrastructure related organisations.
Strong understanding of governance, risk management, internal controls, and regulatory expectations within highly regulated environments
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and challenge effectively at Executive Committee, Board Committee, regulator, customer, and senior management levels.
Experience engaging with regulators and supporting regulatory reviews, supervisory interactions, and remediation activities within a highly regulated environment
Proven experience presenting to senior governance forums and developing high-quality committee papers, management reports, and strategic insights.
Strategic mindset with the ability to align assurance activities to business priorities, product strategies, organisational objectives, and the evolving payments landscape
Proven track record of leading, developing, and motivating high-performing teams, including talent development, succession planning, and performance management
Extensive experience leading complex technology, business, operational, cyber, resilience, and integrated audits in dynamic and fast-paced environments.
Experience leading change assurance, advisory reviews, and strategic initiatives, providing pragmatic insight while maintaining independence and objectivity
Experience overseeing audit issue management, including tracking, validation, escalation, and driving timely, sustainable remediation of identified control weaknesses.
Ability to identify and communicate thematic risks, emerging control trends, and forward-looking insights
Experience leveraging data analytics, automation, and AI-enabled tools to enhance audit coverage, improve efficiency, and deliver deeper, more actionable insights
Relevant professional qualification (e.g., ACA, CA, ACCA, CIA, CISA, CISSP, or equivalent) with a strong understanding of the Global Internal Audit Standards and a commitment to ensuring audit activities are conducted in conformance with those standards.
Demonstrates a growth mindset and commitment to continuous professional development, actively seeking feedback and opportunities to build on strengths, broaden expertise, and enhance leadership effectiveness.

Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

Job Title
Senior Accountant – UK Controller
Overview
The position reports to the Manager, UK Controller, part of the Europe Regional Controller’s group.
The Europe Controllers Group is responsible for ensuring the integrity of the US GAAP financials in partnership with the GBSC (Global Business Service Center), ensuring local statutory reporting compliance as well as providing support to the business teams across a number of areas including accounting and controls.
The role will cover controller activities in the UK, including support for Mastercard Payment Gateway Services.
The Controller activities include the following:
o Integrity of the Financials - The Controllers work in partnership with their local teams and the GBSC to ensure that the financial statements for their businesses are appropriate. This includes both management reporting and statutory filings.
o Business Advice is provided by the Controllers to ensure the proper accounting and reporting for transactions, customer deals, expenses and other areas.
o The Controllers play a critical role in the First Line of Defence in the Risk and Control Framework. Using the Operational Risk Management (ORM) methodologies and policy, the Controllers ensure that we have efficient processes with effective controls.
Role
Accounting and Internal Controls
Oversee the integrity of the financial records of UK based legal entities in accordance with MasterCard policies in partnership with the GBSC.
Manage the statutory account audits for UK based legal entities on a timely basis as well as provision of quarterly disclosure information to MasterCard Corporate Group;
Maintain strong relationships with external parties (auditors and other third parties involved in the statutory reporting process).
Maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders and be able to assess and communicate key risks and opportunities within the business.
Assist with the preparation of the monthly financial statement monitoring control in preparation of the monthly review conducted by management.
Maintain a strong internal control environment and improve internal controls where necessary to ensure a scalable infrastructure is in place to allow the company to operate and grow effectively while mitigating risk. Ensure continued alignment with MasterCard internal control procedures.
Documentation of financial and business processes throughout the group of companies under scope of responsibility.
Ad hoc support for Tax and treasury activities including preparation of cash flow forecasts and interim accounts as required.
Billing and Commercial Finance
Perform complex maintenance tasks within the billing system (e.g. customer changes, pricing changes) to support business units and finance teams.
Analyse billing data, research trends, identify issues and follow up on or identify resolutions.
Respond to help desk inquiries within the Service Level Agreement [SLA] area of expertise, provide business knowledge and technical/functional support to business units.
Identify opportunities for process optimization within area of responsibility; coordinate with leadership to implement improvements.
Research and resolve production billing issues and incidents; coordinate meetings between Billing and Technology teams to resolve open issues.
Maintain desktop procedures and adhere to controls around revenues and collections.
Perform routine training to internal teams on billing related topics.
All About You
In terms of the performance and personal competencies required for the position, we would highlight the following:
ACA/ACCA/CIMA qualified
Experience with US GAAP and IFRS and UK statutory accounting and reporting requirements.
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or related discipline
Big 10 or Financial Statement Generation Provider experience preferred
Experience of liaising with external auditors
Experience assessing the effectiveness and oversight of operational and financial control implementation
Experience leading process improvement initiatives along with developing procedures for implementation
Sound project management and organizational skills
Strong analytical skills and proficient with Excel ( VBA skills will be an advantage )
Very good communicator
Flexible and able to perform efficiently under tight deadlines
Enthusiastic, hands on, proactive, able to work well independently and in teams
Takes initiative and is result oriented

Title and Summary
Manager, Global SME Market Expansion
Overview
The SME Global Market Expansion team is a newly established unit within Mastercard’s Global SME organization, focused on unlocking incremental SME payment flows in underpenetrated geographies. The team identifies high-potential markets and drives initiatives to expand card usage, acceptance, and share of wallet among small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs).
The Manager, SME Global Market Expansion will play a critical role in setting and executing strategies to accelerate the shift from cash, checks, and wire payments to card-based solutions. This role combines strategy, analytics, and hands-on execution, with clear accountability for commercial outcomes including Gross Dollar Volume (GDV), Net Revenue (NR), and pipeline creation.
Role
Define and execute the SME card conversion strategy across prioritized markets, with a focus on displacing cash, checks, and wires
Own and deliver against commercial targets, including GDV growth, Net Revenue (NR), and qualified pipeline generation
Identify target SME segments, industries, and use cases with the highest card displacement potential
Diagnose key blockers to growth and design actionable solutions
Lead end-to-end execution of growth initiatives: from ideation and business case development to pilot, measurement, and scale
Key Responsibilities
Strategy Development & Commercial Ownership

Director, Partner Success – Business & Market Insights (Global)
Overview
Mastercard Services leverages the company’s unique data, analytics, technology, and expertise to help customers grow, optimize performance, and manage risk. It delivers solutions across areas like fraud and cybersecurity, customer acquisition and engagement, open finance, and business insights—making commerce smarter, safer, and more personalized through data driven products and advisory capabilities. One of our strategic objectives is to diversify our revenue via new distribution pathways, including through Partners. As such, we are increasing our focus around Partner Success to support the growth of both our partner and MA revenue.
We are seeking an experienced Partner Success Manager to effectively manage a portfolio of strategic B2B partners who utilize multiple Mastercard Business and Market insights products or solutions leveraging Mastercard aggregated and anonymized data. The Partner Success Manager will support partners throughout the onboarding process, provide ongoing relationship management, and drive revenue growth through expansions and strategic initiatives. This individual will serve as a partner advocate within a matrixed organization.
The Role
1. Performance, Insights & Governance
Monitor partner performance, product adoption, usage, satisfaction, service levels, and revenue outcomes; identify risks and opportunities using partner feedback and operational data.
Use monitoring, troubleshooting, and analytical tools to synthesize actionable insights, guide decisions, and support future growth.
Establish a consistent governance cadence, including executive-ready quarterly business reviews, performance reporting, action tracking, and escalation management.
Maintain market and addressable-opportunity insights to inform partner plans, prioritization, and strategic recommendations.
Lead a global team of Partner Success managers working with Partners leveraging Mastercard data
2. Cross-Functional Partnership

Ensure a disciplined transition from Business Development to ongoing partner management, accelerating onboarding, speed to first revenue, product implementation, and scalable adoption.
Align partner plans with broader Mastercard account strategies, particularly where end customers are supported by Customer Account Management or other Customer Success teams.
Partner with Marketing to develop collateral, resources, portal content, events, customer summits, and thought leadership that strengthen partner engagement and enablement.
Provide a thought leadership in strategic directions in collaboration with Head of Partnerships and Customer Success CoE
3. Growing the Business and Partner Advocacy
Develop and execute joint growth plans that expand partner relationships, increase product adoption, and grow volume and revenue across existing and new opportunities.
Drive successful renewals and identify expansion opportunities across new products, use cases, end customers, and markets, including Mastercard-influenced opportunities.
Co-create new approaches and go to market with existing partners and collaboration with Mastercard product teams
Engage regularly with partner stakeholders, including senior and C-suite leaders, to communicate value, review business results, resolve concerns, and advance shared priorities.
Represent the voice of the partner internally, translating feedback and market needs into actionable recommendations that improve Mastercard products, services, and partner experience.
Champion Partner Success best practices and contribute to internal initiatives that strengthen service quality, scalability, and partner outcomes.

Title and Summary
SVP, Risk, Core Payments
SVP, Core Payments Risk Management
Who is Mastercard?
Mastercard (MA) is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and innovation, we help individuals, financial institutions, governments and businesses realize their greatest potential.
Overview:
At Mastercard, risk management is fundamental to achieving our strategic objectives and maintaining the trust of customers, regulators, shareholders and employees. Mastercard is committed to the highest standards of integrity, governance and risk management.
The SVP, Core Payments Risk Management, is a senior leadership role within the MA Risk organization, reporting to the EVP, Risk Strategy and Transformation.
The role is responsible for providing independent second-line-of-defense (2LoD) oversight of Mastercard’s Core Payments business’ risk profile, governance framework, risk culture and control environment. They will also have responsibility to act as Chief Risk Officer for Real Time Payments International entities.
Role:
Strategic Enabler to the Business
Enable growth by designing practical guardrails that allow the business to scale with appropriate risk discipline, regulatory credibility and alignment to Mastercard standards.
Supports scaled and controlled growth in Core Payments strategy, supporting new prioritized product launches and initiatives.
Provide executive‑ready risk insights to leadership, supporting prioritization, investment decisions and timely escalation of material risks.
Risk Management & Execution
Lead risk management and operating cadence including governance forums, escalation pathways, issue management and executive reporting.
Oversee execution across all risk domains (e.g., operational resilience, technology/cyber, third‑party, conduct and other enterprise risks) ensuring consistent application of frameworks, standards and controls across all jurisdictions and business lines.
Ensure clear Three Lines of Defense accountability and independent challenge.
Identify latent and emerging risks, aligning with the 1st Line, and translate them into actionable governance, controls and executive decision-making.
Prioritize areas of focus given risk materiality.
Risk Management Program
Design, operate and continuously enhance risk management practices across Core Payments progressing alignment between risk strategy, appetite and business growth, leveraging Enterprise Risk Management and other relevant standards and practices.
Establish and maintain robust risk governance, including clear escalation pathways, risk committees, and decision‑making structures.
Oversee end‑to‑end risk processes, including risk identification, assessment, monitoring and issue management, ensuring risks are effectively mitigated and controlled.
Develop and coordinate risk reporting for senior leadership.
Partner with business and technology leaders to embed disciplined risk‑taking, ensuring risks across operational, credit and technology domains are actively managed in line with risk appetite.
Integration & Culture
Strengthen and scale a vigilant risk and compliance culture, including training, awareness and consistent operating practices.
Support leadership depth, resilient governance and durable operating practices.
Chief Risk Officer for Real Time Payments International
Serve as the primary independent 2LoD risk lead for Real Time Payments International (RTPI) with customers, regulators and supervisory authorities.
Maintain strong and constructive relationships with relevant regulatory bodies.
Support regulatory examinations, reviews, inspections and remediation programs.
Ensure risk management practices comply with applicable regulatory requirements and supervisory expectations.
Provide risk-related assurance to regulators, customers and other stakeholders as required.
Attend regulatory meetings and provide independent risk perspectives and assurance.
Maintain direct and unrestricted access to the entities’ Risk Committees, including authority to independently escalate material risk concerns where necessary.
Is a member of the RTPI Leadership Team.
All About You:
Leadership & Executive Presence
Leadership experience operating at a senior executive level within a complex organization.
Proven people and team management and leadership capabilities and ability to lead and prioritize activity across multiple teams.
Executive presence with ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive alignment in a matrixed environment
Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders while maintaining strong business partnerships.
Proven experience presenting to executive leadership teams and Risk Committees.
Strategic thinker with strong commercial acumen and business judgment.
Ability to operate effectively within complex governance and regulatory environments.
Risk Management Expertise
Deep expertise in enterprise risk management frameworks, governance and risk oversight.
Significant experience in risk management leadership roles within financial services, payments, banking, fintech or other highly regulated industries.
Strong understanding of risk appetite frameworks, risk assessment methodologies and control assurance practices.
Experience in stress testing, scenario analysis, risk quantification and emerging risk management.
Strong understanding of commercial, operational, technology, cyber and strategic risk management.
Governance & Regulatory Experience
Strong command of Three Lines of Defense operating models and risk culture implementation.
Experience operating within regulated and non-regulated entity environments and formal governance structures.
Demonstrated ability to engage credibly and effectively with external stakeholders including regulators, auditors and customers.
Experience working with regulators and supervisory authorities.
Personal Attributes
Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and critical thinking capabilities.
Ability to provide constructive challenge while fostering collaboration and trust.
High levels of integrity, professionalism and sound judgment.
Strong attention to detail combined with the ability to maintain a strategic perspective.
Open, collaborative and inclusive leadership style while maintaining independence and objectivity.
Highly motivated, resilient and results-oriented.
Embodies and demonstrates Mastercard's values and commitment to ethical conduct.

Mastercard::R-292626.title: Senior Specialist, Product Management
Mastercard::R-292626.text:
Our Purpose
Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.
Title and Summary
Senior Specialist, Product Management
Overview
Mastercard's Digital Assets & Blockchain team is seeking a Senior Specialist, Product Management to support the commercialization and market expansion of digital asset and blockchain-based solutions in Europe. This role will contribute to go-to-market execution, partnership development, market analysis, and product adoption initiatives for products including crypto-linked card programs, stablecoin and digital currency BVNK sales enablement, and emerging blockchain solutions.
The ideal candidate is passionate about digital innovation, payments, and emerging technologies, with experience supporting product launches and commercialization initiatives. They are highly collaborative, analytical, and comfortable working across cross-functional teams in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
Role
Product Commercialization & Market Support
Drive the execution of commercialization strategies for digital assets and blockchain solutions.
Conduct consultative solutions based engagement with customers to support sales efforts
Craft product localization strategies, market readiness assessments, and launch activities to support successful market expansion.
Partner with regional and global stakeholders to ensure alignment on commercialization priorities and customer opportunities.
Go-to-Market Execution
Develop go-to-market plans for digital asset products and solutions.
Support sales enablement activities, including value proposition development, customer-facing materials, and internal education.
Coordinate with product, business development, marketing, legal, compliance, and regional teams to drive launch readiness.
Partnership Enablement
Support the identification, onboarding, and management of strategic partnerships focused on one to many distribution opportunities.
Help maintain strong relationships with customers and partners to support product adoption and business growth.
Assist in evaluating partnership opportunities and preparing business cases.
Market Intelligence & Opportunity Analysis
Conduct market research, competitive analysis, and ecosystem monitoring across the digital assets and blockchain landscape.
Analyze customer, market, and industry trends to identify commercialization opportunities and inform strategic priorities.
Support opportunity sizing, market segmentation, and customer targeting efforts.
Performance Tracking & Insights
Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and commercialization metrics to assess product performance and adoption.
Prepare reports, presentations, and recommendations for stakeholders based on market and performance data.
Help identify opportunities to optimize product adoption and commercial outcomes.
All about you
Experience in product commercialization, product management, business development, consulting, strategy, payments, fintech, or a related field.
Understanding of digital assets, blockchain technology, cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, tokenization, or emerging payment technologies.
Curious and fast learner with a passion for supporting product launches, go-to-market activities, partnership initiatives, or business growth programs.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to synthesize market, competitive, and customer insights into actionable recommendations.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a dynamic, cross-functional environment.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
Corporate Security Responsibility
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

Euronext::R27305.title: GateLab - Project & Programme Management Associate
Euronext::R27305.text:
The Project & Programme Management Associate is responsible for coordinating, tracking, and governing assigned projects and programme initiatives across the organisation, ensuring that scope, timelines, milestones, risks, dependencies, actions, and reporting are managed in a structured, transparent, and consistent way.
The role supports the delivery of strategic, product, transformation, and client-related initiatives by working closely with internal teams.
The position is focused on project and programme governance, planning, coordination, reporting, and execution tracking.
The role contributes to improving delivery predictability, internal accountability, cross-functional coordination, and operational efficiency across the project and programme portfolio.
Gross Annual Salary: 40.000 - 45.000 euro
Key Responsibilities:
Manage client projects from initiation to delivery, ensuring alignment with client needs, product specifications, and company strategy.
Support the definition of project scope, objectives, timelines, and deliverables, ensuring compliance with deadlines and quality standards.
Coordinate cross-functional teams (Sales, Product, Development, Application Management & Support) to deliver projects efficiently and effectively.
Identify and manage project risks, dependencies, and issues, ensuring accountability and timely resolution.
Maintain high standards of client success, customer care, and product quality across all engagements.
Contribute to continuous improvement of project management frameworks, tools, and processes.
Uphold confidentiality, compliance, and professionalism in all client and internal interactions.
Provide regular updates and report activities to management.

BSC in Business, Engineering, Computer Science or relevant field.
Minimum 3 years of experience in project management, client delivery, or programme coordination, ideally within financial software, fintech, or trading technology environments.
Proven experience managing multiple concurrent projects with cross-functional teams.
Strong understanding of project management methodologies (Agile, PMI, PRINCE2) and related tools (Jira, Confluence, MS Project).
Familiarity with trading workflows, financial market processes, and software deployment lifecycles.
Knowledge of DevOps, Quality Assurance, and application support processes in software delivery.
Strong analytical skills and ability to interpret technical and business requirements.
Solid understanding of risk management, planning, and change control principles.
Demonstrated accountability, autonomy, and efficiency in managing complex client projects.
Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship management skills.
Strong sense of responsibility, commitment, and attention to detail.
Focus on client success, customer care, and long-term satisfaction.
Team-oriented mindset with an emphasis on collaboration and mutual respect.
Proven ability to meet deadlines and maintain composure under pressure.
High standards of professionalism, confidentiality, and ethical conduct.
Fluency in English and Italian (spoken and written).
Dedication to continuous learning, professional growth, and operational excellence.

AIG::/job/London/Client-Director--12-mon.text:
Join us as a Client Director to grow your career at the forefront of insurance distribution.
Make your mark in Client and Broker Engagement
Our Client and Broker Engagement (CBE) team manages AIG’s major client relationships across all product lines, as well as driving new business activity. The team serves major clients and broker partners through an elevated, personalised experience – our client-centric framework drives a consistent experience and best practice, while allowing flexibility to meet the client’s needs.

Extensive track record of managing major corporate client relationships as a broker, carrier or risk manager.
Experience of corporate insurance programmes both UK and multinational, particularly across main General Insurance products (P&C, Financial Lines, Specialty)
Strong written and verbal communication skills and proven interpersonal skills

Excellent IT skills

Join us as as a Data & Digital Analyst to take your career to the next level with a global market leader.
How you will create an impact
You will support the design, delivery and adoption of data and digital capabilities across the business. This role sits at the intersection of business need, product thinking and platform delivery, working across Talbot’s core data and digital landscape.

AIG::/job/London/International-Head-of-F.title: International Head of Fraud & Recovery
AIG::/job/London/International-Head-of-F.text:
Join us as our International Head of Fraud & Recovery to grow your career at the forefront of insurance claims.
Make your mark in Claims
Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency
How you will create an impact
This position is responsible for managing the overall fraud and recovery program across AIG’s International business. The position requires proven leadership skills in managing a team of regional managers across 5 regions: APAC and China, Europe Middle East Africa, UK, Latin America and Japan.
The scope of the fraud role supports AIG to reduce the potential economic loss to the business through the identification and investigation of suspicious insurance claims or suspicious insurance related activities covering all lines of business.
The scope of the recovery role supports AIG’s strategy of maximizing recovery opportunity whilst minimizing recovery expenses, ensuring that there is consistency with the way recovery activity is enabled, tracked, monitored and reported.
Critical to the success of this position is the ability to engage, lead and inspire a team of fraud, recovery and salvage professionals to continue to deliver high quality results while creating the fraud and recovery capability of the future. This will involve leveraging new technology and skills and developing new and innovative techniques to help support and achieve AIG GI Claims goals, whilst at the same time developing and nurturing an organizational culture aligned to AIG’s defined purpose and values.
Key responsibilities:
Support the execution of the GI Claims Fraud and Recovery strategy, including deployment of global fraud and recovery technology initiatives, portfolio analytics, TPA governance, vendor management, shared services engagement and expense management.
Create and implement strategies to maximise recovery value and mitigate fraud risk aligned to the Global Fraud and Recovery Key Performance Indicators.
Proven ability to build strong networks with claims, underwriting and external stakeholders and have a proven track record of delivering outstanding results.
Support the advancement of the fraud and recovery reporting and portfolio analytics capability to enable timely reporting and to produce valuable insights to key stakeholders.
Drive strong data citizenship on critical data fields within fraud and recovery related tools and systems to develop accuracy of the Key Performance Indicators.
Support and engage in identified data, digital and Gen AI strategies through targeted engagement and knowledge sharing to ensure fraud and recovery capabilities have been incorporated.
Proactively drive an effective communication and engagement process with key stakeholders regarding the fraud and recovery value proposition, results, recommendations and internal/ external trends.
Work with claims and underwriting teams to understand where fraud exposure exists and where recovery opportunity is available.
Collaborate on new growth setups (e.g. TPA/ MGAs), new product designs and customer initiatives through assessing the impact on recovery and inherent fraud risk and ensuring the right operating model is in place.
Assess the performance of the international fraud and recovery vendor panel, ensuring vendor performance is of the highest quality, delivering value with appropriate expense discipline.
Manage the implementation and monitor the effectiveness of the international fraud and recovery training and awareness campaigns for Claims and Underwriting.
Plan, manage and evaluate work of staff; make decisions regarding pay, performance management, development, employment and staffing requirements.
Ensure compliance with all country laws and regulations regarding fraud and recovery best practices, guidelines, reporting and submissions and data privacy requirements.
Function as the AIG liaison and point of contact for Global Fraud Industry associations and regional/country regulators, law enforcement etc. where required.
Manage expenses within established and approved budget guidelines.
What you’ll need to succeed
Extensive knowledge of claims, insurance markets, fraud and recovery legislation and handling processes, along with other relevant data/ compliance legislation.
Connectivity with relevant fraud and recovery industry associations, with demonstrable credibility.
Ability to leverage technology and analytics to achieve goals including experience in the implementation of AI and Machine learning to assess trends and identify opportunities to drive improved results.
Able to lead complex change initiatives with an ability to work to tight timelines when necessary.
Experience and confidence to lead a large, diverse team and engage a geographically dispersed group of stakeholders.
Comfortable working across differing time zones to support engagement of regional fraud and recovery teams and to actively contribute to the global leadership team.
Able to take ownership of their area of responsibility and work with others to win together in both virtual and in person environments, helping to develop and nurture a high-performance culture.
Excellent communication skills with a strong collaborative mindset to influence stakeholders internally within Fraud and Recovery and other key stakeholders (International/Regional/ LOB claims stakeholders, Underwriters, Actuaries, Risk Compliance, Legal, Vendors, Customers etc).

AIG::/job/London/Lead-Analyst----Legal-E.title: Lead Analyst  - Legal Entity Capital Modelling and Production
AIG::/job/London/Lead-Analyst----Legal-E.text:
Join us as a Lead Analyst, Legal Entity Capital Modelling and Production, to take your career to the next level with a global market leader.
How you will create an impact
Reporting to the Head of Legal Entity Capital Modeling and Production, you will support the production processes across Global Risk and the Capital Modeling and Analytics team including the Group Capital Model, two Solvency II approved Internal Models for both UK and Europe, other local legal entity models and support to Talbot models as appropriate.
The Legal Entity capital models for UK and Europe are used in assessment of Capital Adequacy, Portfolio Management, Risk Management, Asset Management and Reinsurance Management and have approval under Solvency II from their respective regulators. In addition, the team maintains other legal entity capital models, currently Canada and Bermuda models, which support local legal entity risk management and Own Risk and Solvency reporting (ORSA) requirements.
Production processes consist of supporting regular updates of all models, including collection of inputs, quality assurance, implementing controls and validation tests, production of results, analysis of change and assisting with presentations. Furthermore, production includes review and optimization of processes via the creation of new tools and automation as required.
Some of the key responsibilities include:
Produce and present model output and changes for key projects to business stakeholders.
Support business partners with use requirements: Risk Officers with updates to Risk Reporting, Risk Appetite monitoring, Stress Testing, ORSA
Capital Management for Overall Capital Assessments
Reinsurance Officers for Reinsurance Adequacy
Market Risk Officers for analytics on the Investment Portfolio
Support the production of quarterly Internal Model baselines for Group, UK, Europe, Canada and Bermuda legal entities for presentation committees or regulators as appropriate.
Support initiatives to integrate production processes across AIG’s Capital Models (including Group and Talbot where appropriate) to achieve a unified annual run calendar, and common working practices and quality assurance leading to greater resilience.
Keep both the Internal Model and Standard Formula up to date with Regulatory Changes, changes in the company’s risk profile and changes in external environment.
Update logs, reports, testing and documentation such as the Technical Issues log, Expert Judgement Log, Sensitivity Testing Report and Model documentation.
What you'll need to succeed
MSc in a quantitative field, Qualified Actuary or equivalent
5+ years of experience in capital modeling for a General Insurance company
Experience in actuarial pricing or reserving is beneficial.
Experience in the regulation of Solvency II in relation to Internal Models and good background knowledge of other related regulatory regimes.
Able to work with senior business partners and Risk Officers, and present model outputs to internal and external stakeholders
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a global team environment
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
Strong quality control and review skills both qualitative and quantitative
Understanding of risk management tools and risk quantification techniques for all risk areas
Ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Experience with capital modeling packages, in particular Igloo, and programming languages such as Python, R, Matlab and VBA would be beneficial

AIG::/job/London/Multinational-Client-Ex.text:
Join us as a Multinational Client Executive to take your career to the next level with a global market leader.
Make your mark in Multinational
AIG Multinational is an exciting business area within AIG that designs, implements and services bespoke multinational insurance solutions for our global customers, empowering our clients and broker partners to navigate complex cross-border risks with confidence and consistency. AIG Multinational professionals have the diverse skills and expertise necessary to deliver customized, compliant and seamless solutions that support our clients’ risk management objectives. You can work alongside a dynamic, multi-disciplinary team to explore and deliver new solutions to meet our customers’ global insurance needs.
How you will create an impact
This is an external broker and client facing role managing an assigned portfolio of Multinational programs working in partnership with product underwriters and distribution. This role supports all major Multinational lines of business.
Key responsibilities include:
Manage and oversee all aspects of the multinational service delivery for the assigned portfolio and be accountable for the multinational client experience.
Coordinate communication and project management across all internal and external stakeholders throughout the program lifecycle
Ensure appropriate design and effective delivery and service of assigned multinational programs.
Provide multinational technical expertise to underwriters to ensure a compliant program structure and design, and adherence to all local regulatory requirements.
Lead the promotion and adoption of the AIG Multinational End-to-End process.
Lead and manage the day-to-day service delivery to ensure the timely issuance of accurate local policy and invoice documentation.
Partner with Product Underwriters to manage the approval of facultative reinsurance panel participants and the collection of compliant reinsurance documentation for all assigned programs.
Engage with multinational claims to ensure timely development of multinational claims bulletins / protocols and support on ad hoc program enquiries.
Partner with underwriting to draft legal documentation for loss sensitive programs and obtain approval from AIG legal counsel.
Monitor performance and escalate where necessary to ensure all agreed Multinational service SLAs are being met.
Manage and partner with Distribution to coordinate periodic Multinational client/program stewardship meetings.
Support the profitable growth of the multinational portfolio by working in collaboration with product and distribution.
Help identify, support, and contribute to internal and external strategies that align our product offerings and grow AIG multinational business.
What you’ll need to succeed
Commercial insurance experience, preferably client facing
Strong technical knowledge of complex multinational programs, including reinsurance structures, with experience of the multinational environment and processes
Client focused with experience working with multinational corporations and dealing with senior client personnel / risk managers
Strong written & verbal communication skills with the ability to build strong relationships with stakeholders
Able to handle multiple priorities, delegate effectively and meet tight deadlines / SLAs
Able to identify operational improvements and gain technical knowledge / experience to carry out those improvements

AIG::/job/London/Senior-Data---Reporting.text:
Join us as a Senior Catastrophe Reporting Analyst in our Exposure Management team to take your career to the next level with a global market leader.
Make your mark in Talbot Underwriting
Talbot operates within the Lloyd's Insurance Market through Syndicates 1183, 2019, S2478 and 2479. With an expert team of highly skilled and experienced underwriters and a balanced, geographically diverse portfolio of business, Talbot has earned a reputation as an industry leading insurance specialist.
Talbot writes a diversified portfolio including Crisis Management, Energy, Financial Lines, Marine, Political Risk, Property and Terrorism. Drawing on our deep industry expertise, Talbot develops tailored insurance solutions that address clients' evolving and often unique needs.

Support the development of Talbot’s views of catastrophe risk and feed into development / validation activities (including linkage into AIG group work streams)
Assist in developing and reviewing the representation of non-nat-cat classes in the Internal Model
Help to develop oversight frameworks and own procedural documentation for the Exposure Management team
Stay up-to-date with industry developments and investigate ways in which we can enhance our data capture
What you’ll need to succeed
Experience in a similar role within the insurance industry
Understanding of cat modelling and exposure management advantageous
Strong coding skills in R and / or Python
Strong SQL skills
Experience of enhancing and automating processes
Strong understanding of insurance concept

Experience of Delegated Authority Practices, essential that there is significant knowledge of Lloyd’s processes/Regulatory requirements

Join us as the Syndicate Financial Controller to take your career to the next level with a global market leader.

This is an exciting opportunity to be Financial Controller of Talbot’s managed syndicates at Lloyd’s and lead an established Syndicate Finance team.
The purpose of this role is to lead the Syndicate Finance team and ensure that the Syndicate reporting (group and regulatory) is completed accurately and to deadline and that the underlying financial accounting processes operate efficiently and effectively.

Lloyd’s financial reporting and controls for the Talbot managed syndicates. Key deliverables include: US GAAP reporting to AIG, including SAP ledger close

Adyen::7342860.text:
Job Application for Enterprise Account Manager, Adyen for Platforms at Adyen
Enterprise Account Manager, Adyen for Platforms
London
Apply
This is Adyen
Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Spotify, Playstation, Ebay, and Tide - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.
For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.
Why you should join the Adyen Account Management team
At Adyen, the Account Management team is critical to the growth and success of our business, as well as expanding the Adyen brand across the globe. Being part of our Account Management team, you’ll manage relationships with innovative international merchants, covering multiple industries and channels. You’ll have the opportunity to work on cross-functional initiatives and projects in a fast-paced, highly entrepreneurial environment with high autonomy. You’ll become an expert in the global payments landscape and level up your skills through our AM Academy.
We are looking for a proactive and adaptable Account Manager to join our team in London. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker with a hands-on mentality; someone who is eager to help the world’s biggest brands grow while changing an industry. You are excited to work with a global, multicultural team in a collaborative manner and help your team succeed. Your focus will be on delivering an outstanding customer experience, finding new opportunities, and driving mutual success for Adyen and our customers.
Enterprise Account Manager, Platforms and Financial Services
Adyen’s value goes beyond Ecommerce and In-Person payments with a broad offering of embedded payments and financial services like issuing, bank accounts and capital; facilitated by Adyen’s global Banking licenses.
As a Platforms Account Manager in London you will educate and lead our merchants through continuous growth enabled by the Adyen for Platforms solution. The focus will be on global SaaS platforms and E-Commerce marketplaces that provide a range of services to SMBs. By leveraging both Adyen’s embedded payments solution and financial services offerings, your role will be to activate new revenue streams for these platforms and build long-lasting partnerships.
The strong partnership focus within Account Management drives innovation, scalability and expansion, enabling our platform partners to build a profitable payments layer into their solutions. You will build long-lasting relationships with the platform partners across multiple departments, acting as a trusted advisor to key stakeholders within the Leadership, Sales, Onboarding, Risk, Finance and Product Teams.
Sounds exciting? Keep reading!
What You’ll Do:
Power the growth of your customer’s platform in multiple channels and regions, by proactively advising on Adyen’s products and services as well as the international payments landscape
Be the strategic payments and financial services adviser for all of your customer’s different departments
Enable Platforms for scalability through products and marketing that fit their strategy and roadmaps
Oversee and Optimise the integration of the platform into various Adyen for Platforms product offerings
Work closely with the other Adyen offices around the globe, with Technical and Sales teams to realize individual and thought-through integrations for platforms based on their needs
Understand the evolving needs of the customer and the market and serve as a feedback loop for Adyen’s product team to help identify improvements and developments for continued innovation
Who You Are:
You have a minimum of 5 years of experience in a client-facing or product management role, ideally B2B dealing with complex enterprise software
Commercial experience working within payments, financial services, marketplaces, or SaaS platforms
A born networker with high energy, self-starter with a proven commercial and organizational strength, entrepreneurial track record and strong negotiation skills
A strategic thinker with excellent project management skills and the ability to lead and manage time-sensitive, cross-functional initiatives in a fast-paced, highly entrepreneurial environment with little supervision
A natural communicator and team player, comfortable driving technical and commercial discussions
A problem solver, naturally curious and comfortable navigating ambiguity to find solutions for technical, commercial, and operational challenges.
A cross functional project manager of commercial, operational, and technical projects
Have a hands-on mentality being able to set the path for your platform merchants and their onboarding, payment, payout and reporting setup, at the same time make smart decisions on prioritization and delegation while looking at short- and long term planning
Our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitments
Our unique approach is a product of our diverse perspectives. This diversity of backgrounds and cultures is essential in helping us maintain our momentum. Our business and technical challenges are unique, and we need as many different voices as possible to join us in solving them - voices like yours. No matter who you are or where you’re from, we welcome you to be your true self at Adyen.
Studies show that women and members of underrepresented communities apply for jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. Does this sound like you? If so, Adyen encourages you to reconsider and apply. We look forward to your application!
What’s next?
Ensuring a smooth and enjoyable candidate experience is critical for us. We aim to get back to you regarding your application within 5 business days. Our interview process tends to take about 4 weeks to complete, but may fluctuate depending on the role. Learn more about our hiring process here . Don’t be afraid to let us know if you need more flexibility.
This role is based out of our London office. We are an office-first company and value in-person collaboration; we do not offer remote-only roles.

Senior Implementation Engineer
As a Senior Implementation Engineer at Adyen, you will lead the design and delivery of mission-critical payment integrations for some of the world’s largest global companies.
You will influence how global enterprises design and operate their payment infrastructure at scale. Your work will directly impact the reliability, performance, and scalability of payment flows used by millions of end customers worldwide.
This role is focused on solving complex, high-scale technical challenges. You will also shape technical direction, influence product evolution, and mentor implementers across the organization.
This position is based in London, and the ideal candidate is both consultative and technical.
You will design and scale highly resilient, high-performance integration architectures while helping raise the technical bar across the implementation organization.
What you’ll do:
Deliver complex, multi-region enterprise integration projects
Design scalable, high-availability architectures for global merchants handling large transaction volumes
Define and ensure technical standards across implementation engineering teams
Act as a strategic technical advisor in both pre-sales and delivery phases, shaping solutions alongside Sales and senior merchant stakeholders
Shape industry standards and the broader ecosystem by defining how large-scale payment architectures are built and scaled
Foster best practices in reliability, scalability, security, and system design (e.g. idempotency, fault tolerance)
Mentor and support Implementation Engineers across the organization
Partner with Product and Engineering to influence platform evolution and new product design
Manage critical escalations and ensure stability of high-scale merchant integrations

12+ years of experience in software engineering or technical consulting with deep API integration experience
Deep system design and distributed systems expertise
Ability to operate as a solution architect and trusted advisor in complex, enterprise environments
Experience contributing to production-level systems with pragmatic engineering trade-offs
Comfortable engaging with senior technical and business stakeholders

Solid decision-making capability in complex and ambiguous environments
Passion for raising technical excellence across teams and organizations

Airwallex::0041178d-9b99-4c6e-9ad0-d8399.text:
ABOUT AIRWALLEX
Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 676,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.
We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.
We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles https://www.airwallex.com/en-us/operating-principles to see it in full.
ABOUT THE TEAM
The Financial Partnerships team at Airwallex is dedicated to building and managing strategic relationships with key financial institutions and fellow fintech partners worldwide. We focus on expanding Airwallex’s payment network, enhancing our product offerings, and driving mutual growth for Airwallex and our partners. We coordinate closely with cross-functional internal and external stakeholders to deliver innovative solutions and ensure our customers have access to the best financial services worldwide. Join a collaborative, high-impact team that values creativity, agility, and results.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
As Senior Manager, Financial Partnerships, Card Issuing & Acquiring, EMEA, you’ll play a pivotal role in scaling Airwallex’s card issuing and acquiring businesses. You’ll be responsible for building and managing partnerships with global card networks (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex, etc.) and regional/local card schemes, facilitating Airwallex’s entry into new markets, and unlocking strategic opportunities with our network partners. You’ll collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to deliver on critical initiatives and represent Airwallex at partner and industry events, helping to build our brand profile with partners and customers. This role is based in London.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Build and manage partnerships with global card networks and local card schemes to support Airwallex’s card issuing and acquiring businesses.
Facilitate Airwallex’s entry into new markets by coordinating network licensing, regulatory requirements, and program implementation.
Identify and execute on strategic opportunities with network partners, including product/feature collaboration, new revenue streams, cost optimization, and co-marketing initiatives, amongst others.
Negotiate and structure mutually beneficial partnership agreements, and oversee the execution of Airwallex’s obligations under these agreements.
Represent Airwallex at partner and industry events, actively building our brand profile with partners and customers.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders (Product, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Commercial) for strategic planning, execution of critical initiatives, business analysis, and communications regarding partnership status and strategy.
WHO YOU ARE
We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
7+ years of experience working with payment networks, card schemes, financial institutions, or other players in the card issuing/acquiring industry.
Deep understanding of card network dynamics, issuing and acquiring business models, and economics.
Proven track record of building and managing strategic partnerships in a fast-paced, technology-led environment.
Strong negotiation, relationship management, and commercial agreement structuring skills.
Experience working with cross-functional teams, including Product, Legal, Compliance, Finance, and Commercial.
International experience—working in multiple markets or managing cross-border relationships.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills—able to connect with stakeholders at all levels and communicate project expectations and progress effectively.
Thrive under pressure—work well in a high-velocity environment with aggressive timelines, constant change, and dynamic priorities.
Creative problem-solving skills and innate curiosity—we’re trying to grow Airwallex exponentially by exploring new business constructs, not just replicating the old models employed by industry incumbents
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Experience at a global, high-growth fintech or pre-IPO startup.
Experience building financial partnerships in a new geography.
Experience with merchant acquiring and/or card portfolio management and optimizing pricing, interchange, and product profitability.
Recognized as an industry thought leader; experience representing your company at industry events.
This job description is designed to attract top-tier candidates by clearly outlining the impact, expectations, and growth opportunities of the role, while aligning with Airwallex’s internal standards and industry best practices.
APPLICANT SAFETY POLICY: FRAUD AND THIRD-PARTY RECRUITERS
To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com http://airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com http://careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.
Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY
Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. Experience with structured sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC is preferred.
Proven track record of exceeding commercial targets, with demonstrated success in high-target, high-pace environments and consistently delivering against revenue and commercial KPIs.
Strong analytical and strategic skills, with the ability to use data to shape account strategy, identify growth opportunities, and build effective QBRs and account plans.
Proven experience managing complex, multi-product accounts, including developing and executing strategic account plans to drive retention, adoption, expansion, and long-term customer value.
Strong technical aptitude with solid API knowledge, with the ability to understand complex technical requirements, identify customer needs, and work across products to develop appropriate solutions. API knowledge is a must.
Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, with strong verbal and written English and the ability to build credibility and influence across technical, commercial, and senior customer stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to build strong customer relationships and deliver exceptional customer outcomes, acting as a trusted advisor and strong advocate for the customer.
Strong problem-solving, networking, and commercial judgment, combined with resilience, a positive attitude, and a strong bias towards action when navigating internal and external blockers.

Experience with Salesforce highly regarded.

Deep technical understanding of API design principles, security, and developer experience.
Experience considering both user requirements and commercial strategy to drive meaningful product growth.
Strong ability to manage trade-offs between long-term vision and short-term execution.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey product strategy to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Comfortable working in data-driven, cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, global environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Flexibility to work across multiple time zones and with global teams.
Exceptional English and Chinese communication skills are highly valued.

Experience with global card networks (Visa, Mastercard, Amex) and banking partners.
Familiarity with OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman, GitHub, or API client tooling.
Hands-on experience as a developer is a plus.
Knowledge of regulatory compliance, KYC/AML, and card network rules.
Experience in hyper-growth startup environments, financial infrastructure, or technology.
Master’s degree in a relevant field.

Collaborate cross-functionally to strengthen the commercial operating rhythm, including SKOs, training cadences, and feedback loops.
Analyse funnel performance and sales data to surface gaps, inform enablement priorities, and guide coaching efforts.

Highly organized, able to manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Self-starter mentality with a high degree of motivation to understand root causes and deliver success.

Experience working with Salesforce (or similar CRM) and modern sales technology stacks (e.g., Gong, Outreach, Highspot, LMS platforms, AI tools).

Experience in a high-growth fintech or technology scale-up environment.
Experience working with EMEA-based sales teams.
