WHAT YOU’LL DO
The Customer Success Manager role is a key commercial operations role at Airwallex as we continue to rapidly grow in EMEA. This role will work with our commercial team on our SME/MM clients through the implementation, go-live and servicing phases. You will work cross functionally, engaging with many teams across the Airwallex family including sales, solutions engineering, account management and operations. Furthermore, you are a technology-minded, fintech enthusiast who is driven by learning the ins and outs of our platform so that you are equipped with the knowledge to solve complex problems. We are looking for someone who has a passion for building relationships, creating amazing customer experiences, and managing the onboarding and customer activation process.
Our UK team is growing, we are currently 110+ employees, working in a hybrid work environment with 3 days per week required in our London Office @wells&more - GPE, Fitzrovia.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Founding member of the CSM team in EMEA to help build out the function
Manage internal operational steps to onboard a client including pricing configuration, client vendor onboarding forms, validating feature configuration pre-launch
Project manage the implementation of new features across the accounts you support
Serve as the escalation point for a customer on any support or technical issues and work closely with Sales, Account Management, Support, Billing, and other Technical teams to ensure resolution
Monitor usage, SLA adherence, failure rates and consult with client and account manager on best practices to improve metrics and success overall
Develop expertise in the product capabilities and leverage that knowledge to understand issues and potential paths to resolve
Ensure client invoices are correctly generated, sent and received by client including additional reporting if necessary
Ensure the best customer experience through proactive identification of issues, proposing solutions and timely communication to acknowledge and keep them informed
WHO YOU ARE
You have at least 5 years of experience in customer success, operations or account management with enterprise clients (advantageous if this is in fintech)
You are a relationship builder - you build meaningful, collaborative relationships with all people that you work with, both internally and externally
You can speak to anyone – you should have exceptional communication skills and be comfortable conversing with people of all backgrounds, domains and seniority level
You are detail obsessed - you check everything upfront twice to make sure there are no downstream impacts due to errors
You are technically minded and have prior experience working in an organization delivering/ troubleshooting SaaS or technical solutions to clients
Experience in payments is desirable
Experience using any of the following tools: Google Suite, Salesforce CRM, Sequel, Google Looker, Zendesk.

Fiserv::/job/Milan-Italy/Senior-Business.text:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Senior Business Analyst
About your role:
You will play a crucial role in leading requirements discussions with clients and finalizing business needs from merchant acquiring banks or financial institutions. This role, based in our Milan office, is vital in ensuring successful delivery of comprehensive solution documents and facilitating strong relationships with internal stakeholders and third parties.
The Business Analyst, Merchant Solutions, is responsible for working closely with clients, product teams, technology teams, and third-party partners to gather, analyze, and document business requirements for merchant acquiring and payment solutions. The role serves as a bridge between business stakeholders and delivery teams, ensuring client requirements are translated into scalable, efficient, and compliant payment solutions.
This position requires strong expertise in merchant acquiring, payment processing, card schemes, payment gateways, switching, settlement, reconciliation, and related value-added services
What You’ll Do:
Draft end-to-end merchant acquiring solutions for banks or financial institutions.
Gather requirements, identify appropriate solutions, and ensure successful implementation of merchant solutions
Identify, analyze, research, and resolve functional queries from internal teams and third parties
Ensure the prompt resolution of moderate to complex queries from internal teams and external partners
Interact and communicate effectively with various internal departments
Utilize knowledge of acquiring solutions, platforms, systems, and technical expertise
Act as a consultant, understanding system parameters and options
Identify systemic and business-impacting trends and escalate through proper leadership channels
Experience you’ll need to have:
Extensive SME Functional knowledge in Merchant Acquiring Solutions covering payment gateway, authorization switches, scheme clearing & settlements, merchant pricing, interchange and scheme fees, financial reconciliations
Fluent in Italian & English
Prior experience working within the payments industry
Salary starting at €60,300 - negotiable depending on experience
Thank you for considering employment with Fiserv. Please:
Apply using your legal name
Complete the step-by-step profile and attach your resume (either is acceptable, both are preferable).
Our commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other category protected by law.
Note to agencies:
Fiserv does not accept resume submissions from agencies outside of existing agreements. Please do not send resumes to Fiserv associates. Fiserv is not responsible for any fees associated with unsolicited resume submissions.

Fiserv::R-10399414.text:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Operational Business Analyst
About your role:
Reporting to the Programme Director and/or Programme Manager, the role of Operational Readiness Business Analyst is to support client implementations, conversions and migration initiatives by assessing, documenting and coordinating the operational readiness activities required to enable a successful transition into go-live, warranty and business-as-usual.
Working closely with clients, internal Fiserv teams and third-party partners, the Operational Readiness Business Analyst helps ensure that operational processes, support models, controls, procedures, training needs and handover requirements are clearly understood, documented and aligned to the target-state solution and implementation plan.
The Operational Readiness Business Analyst is responsible for supporting readiness activities across the full project lifecycle, from initial impact assessment and readiness planning through implementation support, go-live preparation and transition to BAU. The role acts as a key link between business stakeholders, operations, service and support teams, implementation teams, product, technology and testing teams to help ensure that operational teams are prepared for change and able to support the target operating model effectively.
Within this context, the role requires a good understanding of issuing and card-processing environments, operational processes and the practical impacts of migrating from legacy platforms to modern target solutions.
What you will do:
Supporting the definition and coordination of the operational readiness approach in alignment with project and implementation objectives.
Assessing current-state and target-state operational processes to identify readiness impacts, gaps, dependencies and required changes.
Gathering, analysing and documenting operational readiness requirements across business, service, operations and support teams.
Supporting the identification of impacts to operating procedures, service models, controls, escalation paths, support processes and business continuity arrangements.
Producing and maintaining readiness documentation, including impact assessments, readiness trackers, process documentation, handover requirements and supporting artefacts.
Working closely with implementation, business analysis, product, technology, testing and operations teams to ensure that readiness activities are aligned to the broader programme plan.
Supporting the definition and tracking of readiness criteria for key milestones, go-live and transition to BAU.
Coordinating with stakeholders to ensure that process changes, support requirements, operational dependencies and handover activities are clearly understood and planned.
Supporting training needs assessment and readiness-related communications for impacted teams where required.
Identifying, analysing and resolving operational readiness queries raised by stakeholders, internal teams and third-party partners.
Supporting go-live preparation by ensuring that operational teams, processes and support arrangements are ready for transition.
Acting as a liaison between business, operations, service/support teams and project delivery teams throughout the readiness lifecycle.
Execution & Controls
Managing and maintaining operational readiness deliverables in accordance with established Fiserv governance, standards and project methodology.
Supporting the planning, prioritisation and tracking of operational readiness activities in line with project milestones, implementation phases and delivery timelines.
Ensuring that readiness requirements, dependencies, actions and open points are captured, tracked and progressed to closure.
Maintaining operational readiness trackers and supporting the assessment of readiness status across impacted teams and functions.
Working with stakeholders to validate readiness criteria, handover requirements and support arrangements prior to go-live.
Participating in governance meetings, working sessions and status reviews to provide updates on readiness progress, key issues, risks and unresolved dependencies.
Escalating readiness risks, gaps, blockers or delivery concerns to the appropriate stakeholders in a timely and structured manner.
Supporting implementation and testing activities where operational readiness input is required, including business process validation and handover readiness.
Supporting warranty and BAU transition planning by ensuring that support teams, processes, documentation and responsibilities are clearly defined and agreed.
Maintaining clear and consistent communication with clients, internal teams and third parties on operational impacts, readiness actions and transition requirements.
Closeout & Transition
Confirming that operational readiness requirements and agreed handover activities have been completed and transitioned appropriately into go-live, warranty and BAU support processes.
Supporting the completion and archiving of readiness documentation, including process updates, handover artefacts and supporting records.
Assisting with post-implementation reviews to assess readiness outcomes, operational issues and improvement opportunities.
Ensuring that outstanding readiness actions, process gaps or follow-up items are tracked through to closure or transitioned appropriately into warranty and BAU support processes.
Contributing to Lessons Learned activities where applicable.
Experience you’ll need to have:
Proven experience (minimum 5 years) in one or more of the following areas: Operational Readiness, Service Readiness, Business Process Change, Operations, Customer Servicing, Testing, Training, and BAU Handover within the Financial Services industry, in the Cards and Payments sector; experience in card and/or payment processing environments is preferred.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with professional proficiency in both English and Italian.
Good understanding of implementation lifecycles, go-live readiness, handover processes and transition to BAU.
Working knowledge of issuing, card-processing and payments operations, with an understanding of how operational requirements translate into service and support.
Experience that would be great to have:
Business Analysis, Change Management or Project Delivery certification preferred.
Experience supporting migrations from legacy platforms to modern processing platforms.
Experience working on multi-country programmes and complex client delivery initiatives.
Exposure to operational change, support model design or business readiness activities within issuing or payments environments preferred.
Salary starting at €52,470 - negotiable depending on experience

Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Business Analyst
About your role:
Reporting to the Programme Director and/or Programme Manager, the role of Business Analyst is to support client implementations, conversions and migration initiatives by gathering, analysing and documenting business and functional requirements in line with programme objectives and delivery needs.
Working closely with clients, internal Fiserv teams and third-party partners, the Business Analyst plays a key role in ensuring that business needs are clearly understood, translated into structured functional requirements and aligned to solution capabilities, operational processes and target-state outcomes.
The Business Analyst is responsible for supporting analysis activities across the full project lifecycle, from initial requirements definition and current-state assessment through functional documentation, testing support, go-live readiness and transition to BAU. The role acts as a critical link between business stakeholders, subject matter experts, implementation teams, product, technology and testing teams to help ensure that solutions are delivered in line with business, operational and technical requirements.
Within this context, the role requires a solid understanding of issuing and card-processing environments, including client servicing, operational processes and the impacts of migrating from legacy platforms to modern target solutions.
What you’ll do:
Leading business and functional requirements discussions with clients, internal stakeholders and subject matter experts to gather, validate and document project needs.
Analysing current-state and target-state processes to identify functional gaps, operational impacts, dependencies and areas requiring clarification or design decisions.
Defining and documenting business requirements, functional requirements, process flows, business rules, user stories and other supporting analysis artefacts.
Translating business needs into clear, structured and actionable functional requirements for implementation, product, technology and testing teams.
Supporting solution definition activities by working closely with SMEs, implementation teams, product teams and technical teams to assess options and recommend appropriate functional approaches.
Producing and maintaining analysis documentation across the project lifecycle, including requirements packs, functional specifications, gap analysis, decision logs and process documentation.
Developing and maintaining requirements traceability to ensure approved requirements, changes and decisions are tracked and aligned to delivery outcomes.
Supporting the documentation of the overall functional approach, including impacts to client processes, operational models, controls and target-state solution design.
Identifying, analysing, researching and resolving functional queries raised by internal teams, clients and third-party partners.
Supporting impact assessments related to process changes, regulatory and compliance requirements, operational readiness and implementation activities.
Working closely with issuing, card-processing and operational stakeholders to ensure that business priorities, processing requirements and client expectations are clearly understood and reflected in the solution.
Supporting readiness activities by ensuring that requirements, process impacts, decisions and functional dependencies are clearly understood by all relevant stakeholders.
Acting as a key liaison between business stakeholders and delivery teams throughout the implementation lifecycle, ensuring clear communication and alignment at all stages.
Execution & Controls
Managing and maintaining business analysis deliverables in accordance with established Fiserv governance, standards and project methodology.
Supporting the planning, prioritisation and delivery of business analysis activities in line with project milestones, implementation phases and delivery timelines.
Ensuring that requirements are reviewed, validated, approved and baselined in line with agreed governance processes.
Tracking requirement changes, open points, assumptions, dependencies and key decisions throughout the lifecycle of the project.
Supporting the creation and maintenance of functional documentation required for implementation, testing, readiness and go-live activities.
Working with implementation, product, technology and testing teams to ensure requirements are fully understood and correctly translated into solution design and delivery outputs.
Supporting testing activities by reviewing test scenarios, validating coverage against requirements and assisting with defect analysis, functional clarifications and issue resolution.
Supporting user acceptance testing, operational readiness assessments and go-live preparation from a functional and business process perspective.
Participating in governance meetings, status reviews, workshops and working sessions to provide updates on analysis progress, requirement status, key decisions and unresolved issues.
Escalating risks, issues, requirement gaps or delivery concerns to the appropriate stakeholders in a timely and structured manner.
Maintaining clear and consistent communication with clients, internal teams and third parties on requirements, impacts, decisions and functional changes.
Supporting implementation events and critical project milestones by providing functional expertise and analysis support where required.
Closeout & Transition
Confirming that business and functional requirements have been delivered, validated and transitioned appropriately into implementation, testing, warranty and BAU support processes.
Supporting the completion of final documentation and ensuring that approved requirements, decisions and analysis artefacts are archived appropriately.
Assisting with the review of implementation outcomes, requirement coverage, defects and lessons learned to identify opportunities for improvement.
Ensuring that outstanding functional queries, requirement gaps or follow-up actions are tracked through to closure or transitioned appropriately into warranty and BAU support processes.
Contributing to post-implementation reviews and Lessons Learned activities where applicable.
Experience you’ll need to have:
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with professional proficiency in both English and Italian.
Working knowledge of issuing, card-processing and payments operations, with an understanding of how business requirements translate into processing and operational outcomes.
Subject Matter Expert / Business Analyst experience in one or more of the following areas strongly preferred: Regulatory, Compliance, Payment Schemes, Card Processing, Customer Correspondence, Fulfillment, Collections, Risk/Fraud, Disputes, Chargebacks, Retrievals, Testing, Consumer Finance, Credit Cards, Loans, Debit Cards and Retail Cards.
Significant proven experience in business analysis, requirements gathering, functional analysis or solution analysis roles, within the Financial Services industry, in the Cards and Payments sector; experience in card and/or payment processing environments is preferred (6-10 years).
Proven experience supporting and/or leading business analysis activities for medium to large client-facing implementations, conversions or migration initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and workstreams.
Experience that would be great to have:
Business Analysis certification or equivalent professional training preferred.
Experience in issuing, card-processing or broader consumer finance environments strongly preferred.
Experience supporting migrations from legacy platforms to modern processing platforms.
Experience working on multi-country programmes and complex client delivery initiatives.
Exposure to regulatory, operational or processing change initiatives within issuing environments preferred.
Salary starting at €52,470 - negotiable depending on experience

Fiserv::R-10399420.title: Senior Business Analyst
Fiserv::R-10399420.text:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Senior Business Analyst
About your role:
This is a leadership role that demands deep payments domain expertise, exceptional client-facing skills, the ability to navigate ambiguity in complex programmes, and a track record of leading analysis workstreams in large-scale regulated environments.
The ideal candidate will bring strong consultative skills honed through direct client engagement, the confidence to shape solutions where requirements are unclear or evolving, and the ability to mentor and lead other analysts. They will also demonstrate the practical application of AI in business analysis, including the use of AI-enabled tools to accelerate requirements gathering, improve documentation quality, automate analysis tasks, and enhance traceability and validation.
What you’ll do:
Leadership & Client Engagement
Act as a trusted adviser to senior client stakeholders, building and maintaining strong relationships at Director and VP level.
Lead and mentor a team of business analysts, setting standards for quality, consistency, and delivery.
Own the analysis workstream end-to-end, taking accountability for scope, quality, and timely delivery of all BA outputs.
Represent the programme in client-facing governance forums, steering committees, and executive reviews.
Navigate ambiguity confidently — proactively clarifying scope, surfacing assumptions, and driving decisions where requirements are incomplete or conflicting.
Influence and negotiate with stakeholders across organisational boundaries to align priorities and resolve competing demands.
Coach junior analysts in structured thinking, stakeholder management, and payments domain knowledge.
Requirements Gathering & Business Analysis
Lead discovery workshops with business stakeholders, technology teams, and external partners to elicit, analyse, document, and validate business and functional requirements.
Analyse existing credit card issuing and processing workflows, identify gaps, and define future-state requirements aligned to migration objectives.
Decompose complex, ambiguous business problems into structured, actionable requirements — even where source documentation is limited or stakeholder views conflict.
Leverage AI-assisted tools to accelerate requirements discovery and summarisation, improve consistency and quality of requirement definitions, and support impact analysis and dependency identification.
Ensure requirements are clear, testable, traceable, and aligned with business outcomes.
Proactively identify risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies (RAID) and escalate appropriately.
Migration Analysis & Planning
Lead the design and execution of credit card platform migration strategies, ensuring minimal customer and operational disruption.
Define and validate data mapping, transformation rules, reconciliation requirements, and cutover dependencies.
Drive planning and validation of parallel runs, rehearsals, and migration checkpoints, with a focus on data integrity and regulatory compliance.
Anticipate downstream impacts and dependencies across multiple workstreams, proactively managing cross-functional alignment.
Process & Functional Documentation
Produce and own high-quality business process models, functional specifications, migration artefacts, and data definitions.
Maintain end-to-end requirements traceability from business need through design, build, and test.
Use AI-enabled documentation tools to improve accuracy and completeness, reduce manual effort, and identify inconsistencies or gaps across requirement sets.
Establish documentation standards and templates for the BA team.
Testing, Validation & Readiness
Define UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with client and delivery teams.
Oversee User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and system integration testing activities related to migrated functionality.
Validate migrated data, business rules, and processing outcomes against defined requirements.
Ensure solutions meet security, regulatory, and operational readiness standards.
Stakeholder & Delivery Collaboration
Act as the primary liaison between business units, technology teams, delivery partners, and vendors.
Drive project leadership with status reporting, impact assessments, risk identification, and decision papers.
Contribute to governance forums and working sessions with clear, data-driven insights and recommendations.
Build consensus across diverse stakeholder groups, managing expectations and resolving conflict constructively.
Experience you’ll need to have:
Experience leading and mentoring BA teams (3+ analysts) on complex programmes.
Deep understanding of credit card issuing, processing platforms, and payment ecosystems (8+ years in payments or financial services).
Strong hands-on experience with VisionPLUS / FirstVision platforms for credit and debit card management.
Experience with leading card processing platforms (FirstVision, CMS, TSYS, etc.).
Knowledge of ISO 8583 messaging, APIs, and service-based integrations in card processing.
Experience with BPM/process modelling tools (e.g., Visio, Miro, Lucidchart).
Familiarity with data analysis tools (SQL, Excel advanced, Power BI).
Multiple platform migration or major transformation programmes within payments or financial services.
Working knowledge of payments regulatory requirements, including PCI DSS, PSD2, and local regulations.
Experience that would be great to have:
Professional certifications (e.g., CBAP, PMP, payments-specific certifications) are highly desirable.
Salary starting at €77,670 - negotiable depending on experience

Fiserv::R-10399425.title: Implementation Manager
Fiserv::R-10399425.text:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Implementation Manager
About your role:
Reporting to the Programme Director and/or Programme Manager, the Implementation Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating and delivering client implementations, conversions and migration initiatives to meet specified business needs, while managing resources from multiple areas (and potentially third parties) to achieve agreed time, quality and client readiness objectives.
The Implementation Manager has accountability and responsibility for the successful delivery of implementation activities across the full lifecycle, from initial planning and requirements alignment through testing, go-live and transition to BAU. The role acts as the key coordination point between the client, internal Fiserv teams and external partners to ensure that solutions are implemented effectively and in line with business, operational and technical requirements.
What you’ll do:
Defining the implementation approach, scope and delivery plan in alignment with client and programme objectives.
Setting client expectations with respect to implementation deliverables, milestones, dependencies, timelines and readiness activities.
Establishing an appropriate implementation governance structure, in line with the Fiserv programme/project methodology and governance framework.
Supporting the client and sponsor through implementation planning, key decisions, sign-offs and readiness checkpoints.
Documenting the overall implementation approach, including conversion strategy, cutover planning, testing phases and transition requirements.
Developing and maintaining detailed implementation workstream plans across the full programme lifecycle, ensuring deliverables, walkthroughs, sign-offs and timeline dependencies are clearly defined and tracked.
Developing estimates for resources, effort and durations and, based on these, creating a high-level implementation schedule and requesting appropriate resources.
Facilitating the development of all elements of the implementation plan, including scope, schedule, RAID management, testing, training, communications, cutover and transition to BAU.
Establishing and managing event readiness criteria and readiness tracking across Fiserv, client and third-party workstreams, including RAG status reporting and escalation of at-risk items.
Defining and coordinating event governance, communications and the Schedule of Events (SoE), including checkpoint strategy, decision point criteria, meeting cadence, attendees, decision makers, cutover activities, dependencies, task sequencing and client alignment.
Ensuring that all implementation impacts on business processes, operational readiness and business continuity are assessed and continually monitored throughout the implementation lifecycle.
Coordinating cross-functional Fiserv teams, client stakeholders and third parties to ensure alignment on activities, deliverables and dependencies.
Acting as a primary point of contact for the client during implementation delivery and maintaining strong working relationships across all stakeholders.
Execution & Controls
Managing, maintaining and tracking the overall implementation plan, controls, work assignments, risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies in accordance with established Fiserv governance.
Reporting implementation status, including schedule, risks, issues, milestones, decisions and scope changes, to all stakeholders on a regular basis.
Managing readiness trackers and event entry criteria to assess implementation readiness and support go/no-go decision making.
Organising and facilitating the appropriate governance forums to review progress, manage escalations and determine corrective or preventive actions.
Managing implementation risks and issues, ensuring that team members are actively involved in identification, ownership and resolution activities where appropriate.
Monitoring implementation progress across all workstreams and ensuring that deliverables are completed on time and to the required quality standards.
Building and maintaining a cohesive cross-functional implementation team environment and fostering productive working relationships across Fiserv, client and third-party teams.
Ensuring the development, review and approval of all key implementation deliverables.
Refining resource, effort and duration estimates as the implementation progresses, ensuring that resource requests are raised early enough to secure the required support.
Managing proposed changes in scope, schedule or implementation approach with key stakeholders, clearly communicating impacts and recommended actions.
Scheduling, managing and participating in implementation reviews, testing checkpoints, readiness assessments and go-live planning sessions.
Ensuring the Schedule of Events (SoE) is detailed, baselined and aligned with the client plan prior to implementation events and updated with lessons learned for subsequent events.
Coordinating command and control activities during implementation events, including real-time tracking of task execution, dependencies, slippages and decision points.
Supporting the definition and execution of the event incident management process, ensuring alignment with client processes, Fiserv internal incident management standards, incident priorities and event-related SLAs.
Developing and maintaining event rota, support and contact plans to ensure appropriate coverage, escalation paths and resource availability during implementation and go-live windows.
Organising, leading and motivating a matrix team of Fiserv SMEs and, where applicable, third-party resources.
Maintaining an ongoing dialogue with PMO and programme leadership to ensure that defined processes are followed and that issues are addressed in a timely manner.
Ensuring a clean, structured and fully supported transition to BAU, including appropriate handovers to service and support teams.
Providing out-of-hours cover during critical implementation and go-live windows, including implementation weekends where required.
Performing implementation administration, including status reporting, documentation management, action tracking and governance support.
Closeout & Transition
Obtaining approval from the sponsor and client that implementation acceptance criteria have been met.
Confirming that implementation objectives and agreed deliverables have been achieved.
Confirming that all outstanding implementation risks and issues have been accepted, transitioned or resolved appropriately.
Supporting financial tracking and implementation completion activities, where applicable.
Facilitating the implementation review and obtaining approval to close out the implementation phase, documented within an end-of-implementation report.
Reviewing implementation outcomes, lessons learned and event performance to identify improvements and incorporate actions into future implementation events where applicable.
Ensuring that post-event actions, outstanding items and agreed lessons learned are tracked through to closure or transitioned appropriately into warranty and BAU support processes.
Performing implementation closeout activities and archiving implementation documentation, including the completion and communication of formal Lessons Learned outputs where applicable.
Experience you’ll need to have:
Significant proven experience (minimum 5 years) in implementation management, client onboarding, conversion or delivery roles within the Financial Services industry, in the Cards and Payments sector; experience in card and/or payment processing environments is preferred.
Proven experience coordinating cross-functional teams to deliver medium to large implementations successfully, including full lifecycle conversions or migration initiatives with interdependent resources.
Experience managing implementation deliverables such as readiness trackers, Schedule of Events (SoE), cutover plans, governance checkpoints, decision points, support rotas and post-event lessons learned.
Strong command of MS Office products, especially Word, Excel, PowerPoint and MS Project.
Strong understanding of implementation lifecycles, client onboarding, conversion and go-live processes.
Strong understanding of event readiness management, cutover planning and Schedule of Events (SoE) control.
Good understanding of incident management processes, event governance and operational handover into warranty and BAU.
Ability to manage structured communications, checkpoint governance and decision-making forums during critical implementation events.
Ability to plan and monitor complex implementations consisting of multiple workstreams and delivery endpoints.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills and English/Italian proficiency.
Experience that would be great to have:
PRINCE2 certification or equivalent project/implementation delivery certification preferred.
Experience working on multi-lingual, multi-country projects and willingness to travel for business as required.
Experience supporting platform migrations from legacy environments to modern processing platforms strongly preferred.
Salary starting at €67,500 - negotiable depending on experience

Working closely with clients, senior stakeholders, internal Fiserv teams and external partners, the Project Manager acts as a central point of leadership across delivery activities, ensuring that projects are delivered in line with business, operational and technical requirements, and that stakeholders remain aligned throughout the project lifecycle.
What you’ll do:

Setting client expectations with respect to project deliverables, timelines, plans and governance.
Establishing an appropriate project governance structure in line with the Fiserv programme/project methodology and governance framework.
Supporting the client and sponsor in obtaining the necessary authorisations, approvals and sign-offs for the business case and key delivery decisions.

Organising and facilitating governance forums to review project progress, manage escalations, support decisions and agree corrective or preventive actions.
Managing project risks and issues, ensuring that ownership is clearly assigned and that resolution activities are progressed in a timely manner.

Ensuring that project team members and workstream leads are aligned on priorities, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting requirements and escalation paths.
Building and maintaining a cohesive cross-functional project team environment and fostering productive working relationships across Fiserv, client and third-party teams.
Ensuring the development, review and approval of all key project deliverables and governance outputs.
Refining resource, cost and duration estimates as the project progresses, ensuring that resource requirements for each phase are identified early enough to secure the required support.
Managing proposed changes in scope, schedule or budget with key stakeholders, clearly communicating impacts, trade-offs and recommended actions.
Scheduling, managing and participating in project reviews, quality reviews and key delivery checkpoints, and driving action plans to address issues arising.
Organising, leading and motivating a matrix team of Fiserv SMEs and, where applicable, third-party resources.
Maintaining an ongoing dialogue with PMO and programme leadership to ensure that defined project processes are followed and that issues are addressed in a timely and structured manner.
Ensuring a structured and fully supported transition to BAU, including appropriate handovers to service and support teams.
Providing leadership support during critical delivery milestones, including out-of-hours coverage where required.
Performing project administration, including status reporting, documentation management, financial tracking, action tracking and governance support.
Closeout & Transition
Obtaining approval from the sponsor and client that project acceptance criteria have been met.
Confirming that project objectives and agreed deliverables have been achieved.
Confirming that all outstanding project risks and issues have been accepted, transitioned or resolved appropriately.
Performing comparisons of estimated and actual costs and supporting financial closeout activities.
Facilitating the project evaluation and obtaining approval to close out the project, documented within an end-of-project report.
Performing project closeout activities and archiving project documentation. Where applicable, conducting a formal Lessons Learned session and publishing the results to all stakeholders.
Experience you’ll need to have:
Significant proven experience in project management roles, preferably gained within the Financial Services industry, in the Cards and Payments sector (8+ years).
Strong command of MS Office products, especially Word, Excel, PowerPoint and MS Project.
Strong client-facing communication, stakeholder management and governance leadership skills.
Strong leadership presence, with the ability to influence and align cross-functional teams in a matrix environment.
Strong understanding of project lifecycles, governance, financial control and transition to BAU.
Ability to plan and monitor complex projects consisting of multiple workstreams and delivery endpoints.
Ability to build and maintain a strong network of contacts across the Fiserv organization, interfacing with multiple IT groups, business units and external stakeholders.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with professional proficiency both in English and in Italian.
Experience that would be great to have:
PRINCE2 certification or equivalent project management certification preferred.
Experience in card and/or payment processing environments is preferred.
Proven experience managing complex, medium to large client-facing projects involving multiple workstreams, stakeholders and interdependent resources.
Experience managing full lifecycle projects, including planning, governance, financial control, execution oversight and transition to BAU.
Experience facilitating governance meetings, project reviews and workshops involving internal and external participants, including senior stakeholders.
Experience working on multi-lingual, multi-country projects and willingness to travel for business as required.
Experience supporting migrations from legacy platforms to modern processing platforms.
Salary starting at €67,500 - negotiable depending on experience

Fiserv::R-10399429.title: Senior Programme Manager
Fiserv::R-10399429.text:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Senior Programme Manager
About your role:
This role suits a seasoned delivery leader (15–20+ years' experience) who can own the client relationship at executive level, shape programme direction where clarity is lacking, and drive teams toward outcomes in complex multi-stakeholder environments. The ideal candidate will combine deep payments domain expertise with a forward-thinking approach to AI-enabled delivery — leveraging automation, agentic AI, and data-driven decision-making to transform programme execution.
What you’ll do:
Strategic Client Leadership
Own and develop the client relationship at executive level — acting as a trusted strategic partner, not just a delivery manager.
Lead governance forums, steering committees, and executive reviews with authority and credibility.
Anticipate client needs, proactively shape engagement strategy, and identify opportunities to deepen the relationship and expand scope.
Navigate complex client politics and competing priorities, building consensus and driving alignment at senior levels.
Use AI-supported insights to strengthen client communications, forecasting, and strategic decision-making.
Manage escalations with composure and judgement, maintaining trust even under pressure.
Programme Delivery & Governance
Lead multiple concurrent BAU, change, and transformation programmes with varied scope and complexity — taking full accountability for outcomes.
Own the full delivery lifecycle from initiation through closure, with particular expertise in large-scale card issuing data migration programmes.
Drive migration strategy, rehearsals, cutovers, and rollback planning with rigour and attention to operational risk.
Operate confidently in ambiguous environments — structuring unclear programmes, making decisions with incomplete information, and adapting approach as understanding evolves.
Drive adoption of AI-enabled delivery approaches including automated status reporting, predictive risk and dependency analysis, and data-driven capacity planning.
Ensure all deliveries meet Fiserv quality standards, contractual commitments, and regulatory obligations.
Team Leadership & Capability Building
Build, lead, and motivate cross-functional delivery teams — setting clear expectations and fostering a culture of ownership and accountability.
Mentor and develop project managers and delivery leads within the team.
Champion consistent use of automation and AI tooling across delivery teams to reduce manual effort and improve quality.
Lead by example in adopting modern delivery practices and continuous improvement.
Cross-Functional Coordination
Orchestrate delivery across global, onshore, and offshore teams — ensuring alignment and removing blockers at pace.
Coordinate effectively across Product, Technology, Architecture, Operations, Compliance, and Integration functions.
Work with payment schemes (Visa, Mastercard), third-party vendors, and regulators where required.
Drive cross-programme dependency management and resource optimisation across the portfolio.
Risk, Issue & Change Management
Proactively identify and manage delivery, regulatory, operational, and migration-specific risks — with strong judgement on escalation vs resolution.
Apply AI-assisted risk identification and trend analysis to stay ahead of emerging issues.
Manage scope changes, CRs, and client expectations through robust governance and clear communication.
Ensure compliance with Fiserv standards and regional regulatory frameworks (CBUAE, SAMA, etc.).
Financial & Commercial Accountability
Own programme P&L — tracking budgets, resource utilisation, margin, and commercial exposure.
Use automation and AI-driven analysis to improve forecasting accuracy and cost transparency.
Lead SOW development, effort estimation, and contract negotiations.
Partner with sales and commercial teams to identify growth opportunities within existing accounts.
Manage commercial risk and ensure programmes remain within agreed financial parameters.
Experience you’ll need to have:
15–20+ years of experience in programme or project management within payments, card processing, or financial services technology.
Deep expertise in payments processing, particularly credit card issuing and platform migrations.
Proven leadership of large-scale, multi-stream data migration programmes in the card issuing domain, including card portfolios, customer/account data, transaction and balance migration, cutover planning, parallel runs, and post-migration stabilisation.
Extensive experience managing enterprise clients at C-suite and VP level, with a consultative, trusted-adviser approach.
Strong delivery track record in credit card issuing and large-scale data migration programmes — multiple successful migrations delivered.
Practical experience using AI and automation to streamline delivery, governance, and reporting — beyond assistive tooling into embedded and agentic AI.
Strong understanding of card issuing platforms (VisionPLUS / FirstVision), data flows, and migration risks.
PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, MSP, or equivalent programme management certification.
Experience that would be great to have:
Experience across multiple card processing platforms (FirstVision, CMS, TSYS, Cortex).
Knowledge of ISO 8583 messaging, card scheme certification, and service-based integrations.
Prior experience in management consultancy or professional services delivery.
Experience managing programmes with budgets exceeding $5M.
Familiarity with portfolio management and PMO leadership.
Salary starting at € 77,670 - negotiable depending on experience

Fiserv::R-10401218.title: Solution Lead
Fiserv::R-10401218.text:
Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Solution Lead
About your role:
The Solution Lead – Merchant Solutions is responsible for defining, designing, and leading the delivery of end-to-end merchant acquiring and payment solutions for banks, fintechs, payment service providers, and merchants. The role acts as the primary solution authority across client engagements, providing strategic and functional leadership to ensure successful implementation of acquiring platforms, payment gateways, switching, settlement, and value-added services.
The Solution Lead serves as the key liaison between clients, business stakeholders, product teams, architects, and delivery organizations, ensuring that business objectives are translated into scalable, secure, and commercially viable payment solutions.
What you’ll do
Own the end-to-end merchant acquiring solution across the project lifecycle.
Lead solution architecture discussions and define target-state operating models.
Evaluate client requirements and align them with platform capabilities and product roadmaps.
Design scalable solutions covering: Merchant Acquiring, Payment Gateways, Authorization & Switching, Scheme Clearing & Settlement, Merchant Pricing & Billing, Reconciliation & Reporting, Fraud Management, Digital Commerce & Value-Added Services
Ensure solution compliance with card scheme, regulatory, security, and operational requirements.
Act as trusted advisor for strategic client engagements. Lead client workshops, solution reviews, and executive presentations.
Provide consultative guidance on acquiring transformation, modernization, migration, and market expansion initiatives.
Present solution options, risks, assumptions, and recommendations to client leadership teams.
Experience you’ll need to have:
Extensive SME Functional knowledge in Merchant Acquiring Solutions covering payment gateway, authorization switches, scheme clearing & settlements, merchant pricing, interchange and scheme fees, financial reconciliations.
Analytical skills and understanding industry metrics and trends.
10+ years of experience in Payments, Banking Technology, or Merchant Acquiring.
5+ years in Solution Architecture, Solution Consulting, or Solution Leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex acquiring or payment transformation programs.
Strong customer-facing consulting experience with financial institutions or payment providers.
Salary starting at €69,390 - negotiable depending on experience
